Team —

Legal concerns: the proposed language shifts risk to Redwood in two ways: a) lowering the uptime SLO increases frequency of remedy events; b) a low fixed quarterly cap combined with prepaid money could create collection/disputes over applicability. We should not accept any language that removes our right to reasonable operational mitigations (scheduled maintenance windows, agreed-upon maintenance notifications, required customer cooperation for incident mitigation).

I recommend the following minimal legal protections to include in the redline:
- Explicit carve-outs for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
- A clear metric definition (how availability is measured, which endpoints, sampling window).
- A dispute resolution path for credits with 30-day cure before credit issuance.

If Sales wants the cap at $25k/quarter, Legal will accept it only if Exec signs off on waiver of standard remediation formula and acknowledges the mitigations above.

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts
